note: What the gate content.no-copied-text refuses in our own wording. `symbols` and `marks` travel with copied material. `lists` describes the fingerprint lists under protected/: each line of protected/<framework>.txt is the hash of one run of `window` words of a text whose terms forbid copying it (or that we hold back), so a list can tell that a passage is the publisher's without holding the passage. A list is made with `openlessons fingerprint <file> --window <n> --sample <k>` from a text file that is never committed, and it is proven before it is trusted: a passage of the source planted in a copy of the tree must pass without the list and be refused with it (`proof`). A framework with no list here is guarded by the paraphrase rule and the licence reviewer alone; its record under standards/ says so (`terms.guard`). The lists catch the copied passage; they cannot see a close paraphrase.
